Himālayas
(‘the abode of snow’)
------------------------------------------
Like the गङ्गा among the rivers, the हिमालयस् among the mountains have become an integral part of the Hindu religion, culture and ethos. Even the Ṛgveda (10.121.4) mentions it as reflecting the greatness of God. Over the centuries, the mountain range has been all things to all beings. Its presiding deity is Himavān. His wife is Menā, a daughter of the pitṛdevatās or manes. Maināka (mountain) is his son. Aparṇā (or पार्वती), Ekaparṇā and Ekapāṭalā are his daughters. These three were married to शिव, the sages Asita and जैगीषव्य.
Mount मेरु is said to be situated in the हिमालयस्.
हिमालयस्">Panoramic views of the HimālayasThe हिमालयस् are the source of many rivers such as भागीरथी (Gaṅgā), यमुना, सरस्वती, विशोका and वितस्ता. They are considered as ‘devatīrtha’ (divine rivers) and hence sacred. Many places of पिल्ग्रिमगे are situated in the Himālayan ranges. Some of them are: अमरनाथ, केदारनाथ, बदरीनाथ, Devaprayāga, Gaṅgotrī, Yamunotrī and so on. Badari-kāśrama where the twin-sages नर-नारायण performed severe austerities, is situated here. वेदव्यास is said to have composed all his works here only. The Pāṇḍavas passed through the हिमालयस् in their mahā-prasthāna or final journey to हेअवेन्.
It is the repository of many a rare medicinal plant. The Rāmāyaṇa mentions the famous sañjīvanī herb which was secured by हनुमान् from here.
The Himālaya mountains consist of parallel ranges, 2500 kms. (1500 miles) long and 250 kms. (150 miles) in width. There are 114 peaks which are over 600 metres (20,000 ft.) in height. Seventy-five of them are higher than 7200 metres (24,000 ft.). All these are perpetually snow-clad and shrouded in mist. Fierce winds and avalanches are quite common.
